newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yasuda Trust says mulling subordinated bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Yasuda Trust says mulling subordinated bond issue.

text.p: Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd said on Wednesday it was considering issuing subordinated bonds worth about 30 billion yen in the July to September period to strengthen its capital base.

A Yasuda Trust spokesman said a final decision had yet to be made, but that the bank planned to place the bonds privately with Fuji Bank Ltd, Yasuda Mutual Life Insurance Co (Yasuda Life) and Marubeni Corp,
"The (bond) issue is aimed at strengthening our capital base in the medium- to long-term," he said.
Yasuda Trust had 281.5 billion yen in subordinated bonds outstanding at the end of March, the spokesman said.
The bank's international capital adequacy ratio stood at 9.86 percent at the end of March.

Fuji Bank, Yasuda Life and Marubeni as well as Yasuda Trust belong to the same Fuyo group, one of Japan's six major groups of companies. Firms belonging to the same groups are generally linked by cross-shareholdings and long-term business ties.
Yasuda Bank plans to strengthen business cooperation with its group companies ahead of Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulation, the spokesman said.
However, the bank had not been considering the establishment of a holding company with group firms, he said.
Japan last month lifted a decades-old ban on holding companies -- firms which control one or more other firms but do not themselves engage in a specific business.
